Households providing food and lodging along routes depended on customers, fuel and grain. Travelers asked about price, space for animals and length of stay. Fermented honey drinks and cooked meals cost resources, while news traveled with their customers. Travelers tended mounts and dried clothes before resting and agreed who watched belongings. Drinking quarrels damaged hospitality while escorts still needed alert guards.

Paying providers helped sustain hospitality for later envoys and patrols.
